caption: Average Change in INC score from combined layer to base layer, where a negative score means the base layer was better than the combined one and vice versa. The gray and orange bars indicate whether the input to the compression layer is inferred frames or lexical signal, respectively. In all cases, inferred frames has a better effect on base layer and lexical signal has improved combined layer's performance.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the average change in INC score when transitioning from a combined layer to a base layer, categorized by observation probability and input type. The horizontal axis represents observation probability, labeled from 0.2 to 0.9 in increments of 0.1, and appears to be linearly scaled. The vertical axis represents average change using compression signal, labeled from -3 to 2 in increments of 0.1, and also appears to be linearly scaled. For each observation probability value, there are two bars presented side-by-side representing ‘Inferred Frames’ colored dark gray, and ‘Lexical Signal’ colored light orange. At an observation probability of 0.2, the ‘Inferred Frames’ bar extends to approximately -2.6 and the ‘Lexical Signal’ bar reaches approximately 0.8. At an observation probability of 0.9, the ‘Inferred Frames’ bar reaches approximately -1.5 and the ‘Lexical Signal’ bar goes to roughly 1.6. The bars are arranged in ascending order based on observation probability. No bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, outlining, or annotations.
